rv.q: My First Ex-Husband is witty, quick and ceaselessly funny.
My First Ex-Husband is a tonic for broken hearts and love-struck audience members alike, healing romantic wounds and working through the complications of love, life, and friendship with laughter.
The result is something along the lines of Nora and Delia Ephron’s “Love, Loss, and What I Wore,” but with less sartorial detail and more whining.
While not a groundbreaking work of theater, My First Ex-Husband is sure to provoke more stories on the drive home as theatergoers reminisce about their own starter marriages.
But the laughs are too few and very far between in My First Ex-Husband, an episodic play composed of eight meandering monologues, all of which could use some level of cutting or restructuring.
The nuance brought a lot of joy and wisdom.

What My First Ex-Husband has going for it is its cast, all expert comedians or actors, who deploy their comic timing, dramatic flair, onstage personality or a combination thereof to uplift the material.
This is a story of survivors, not champions.

My Ex-Husband is the sort of show for women who’d just as soon dress up for a night out and skip the theater, instead plopping themselves in a noisy cafe to eavesdrop on the juicy stories of nearby patrons spilling all the dirt about their lives.
Overall, “My First Ex-Husband” was an engaging, liberating, and entertaining play.

cn.t: Behar's divorce-themed monologue show draws laughs from its talented cast but receives mixed reviews, with critics split between those charmed by its church-like communal energy and those finding it more dishy than dramatically satisfying.
